text:
maria: quick heads-up 1: saw p99/p99.9 token latency spikes during a burst from tenant 'horizon' (peak ~900 r/s). Trace points to long coalesce waits right after our window-compaction change. Thinking about adding an "elastic spill buffer" as a light-weight overflow layer instead of immediate eviction. anyone have strong objections?

kevin: can you share the trimmed span? I want to see enqueue vs wait vs dispatch.

maria: span (trimmed):
```
enqueue: 2ms
coalesce: 16ms
batch_wait: 310ms  <-- long tail
gpu_dispatch: 6ms
kernel: 20ms
```
This lines up with compaction pauses where the batcher squeezes queues.

jasmin: compacting helps avg throughput but if it causes a long pause for a subset of requests that hit the eviction path, the tail explodes. Elastic spill sounds reasonable as it lets us defer work.

rui: proposal sketch: when main coalesce capacity is saturated, place overflow into a per-tenant ring spill with short TTL (e.g., 40ms). The spill uses a non-linear admit probability p = max(p_floor, 1 - occupancy^2) to favor admitting when nearly empty but throttle aggressively when full.

derek: why non-linear? logistic gives sharper knee so we avoid lots of churn on mid-occupancy. Also reduce CPU churn by limiting requeues.

maria: drain semantics: when forming a dispatchable batch, pull up to M entries from spills honoring an ordering: 1) earliest explicit deadline, 2) earliest synth-deadline, 3) fairness round-robin across tenants. each tenant gets at most T tokens drained per dispatch to prevent noisy neighbors.

kevin: how do we synthesize deadlines? we don't want callers to need to change.

jasmin: synth-deadline = now + base_budget * size_ratio * synth_fraction (config). For small requests set tighter deadlines so they don't sit in spill for long. Also allow callers to pass x-req-deadline to opt-in.

rui: KV cache notes: currently eviction from main_queue causes KV-pin churn since some enqueued requests already registered KV pins. If we spill instead of evicting we avoid extra pin/unpin ops. We should carry a kv_fingerprint in the spill entry so if a spilled request moves to slowpath we can decide whether to reload KV or reuse existing entry.

derek: observability: add these metrics per-tenant: spill_in, spill_out, spill_promote_slowpath, spill_rejoin_fastpath, avg_spill_hold_ms, spill_overhead_cpu_ms, drain_tokens_used. Add a histogram for batch_wait_by_spill_state.

maria: cost/tradeoffs list I want to call out:
- pro: significant p99 reduction in unit tests; avoids heavy eviction churn and KV thrash
- con: extra CPU copy/hops; memory need for ring buffers (we have ~64MB spare per GPU but must guard for multi-tenant worst-case)
- con: implementation complexity around fairness + deadline mixing

kevin: perf experiment notes: I ran a synthetic burst with naive spill (no fairness, TTL 40ms, simple admit linear prob) across 100k requests:
- baseline 99.9th: 710ms
- naive-spill 99.9th: 230ms
- p50 ~ unchanged, p90 slightly better
- CPU user increased +6%
- but in 3-tenant noisy scenario one tenant starved sometimes 

jasmin: that matches our expectations. Add drain token caps and deadline prioritization to avoid starvation. Also ensure spill_cap_per_tenant to bound memory.

rui: API surface / runtime knobs to expose in console: enable_spill (bool), spill_soft_limit_pct, spill_ttl_ms, spill_cap_per_tenant, drain_tokens_per_dispatch, synth_deadline_frac, admit_p_floor. Allow overrides per-tenant for enterprise tiers.

derek: rollout plan (deploy-bot please note): feature flag gated; small canary (5% hosts) -> observe p99/p99.9 and CPU delta -> 25% -> 100%. Telemetry required.

deploy-bot: checklist created: feature-flag runtime.elastic_spill, telemetry hooks required, alert if spill_promote_slowpath_rate > 1% for any tenant, canary auto-rollback if p50 regresses >5%.

maria: next actions:
- Rui: implement spill ring + kv_fingerprint tagging + admit prob curve (PR)
- Jasmin: add synth-deadline algorithm + allow header override (PR)
- Kevin: extend telemetry + dashboards + synthetic multi-tenant harness (PR)
- Derek: add console knobs + entitlement override (PR)
- Maria: write short RFC addendum describing API, signals and canary plan

kevin: timeline: aim for experimental canary in 10 business days. I'll run stress with mixed tenant mixes and track CPU cost.

jasmin: note: add unit tests for spill TTL expiry behavior and ensure we don't keep references longer than TTL (memory safety).

maria: good call. Also let's record a microbenchmark comparing spill vs immediate-evict on KV hits/misses so we can quantify the net KV savings.

derek: sounds good. I'll create the console feature flag entry and the telemetry dashboards.

maria: thanks all. If we see regressions in p50 we roll back the flag; otherwise proceed. :thumbsup:
